transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-12
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE); Jonas Meyer (Redwood SE); Dr. Elena Ruiz (Lyricon CDO); Marcus Hsu (Head Eng); Priya Nair (Privacy Counsel); Leo Grant (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): discuss soc two docs, iso, kms, and no train, pilot.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, um introduce ourselves quickly. i'm samira, ae at redwood inference.
[00:12] Dr. Elena: hi all, elena here. quick ask — legal and privacy want ironclad confirmation about training, and we want to see SOC 2.
[00:22] Jonas: hey elena, jonas from solutions eng — we'll cover architecture, kms, and the pilot. quick note, apologies if audio is rough.
[00:32] Marcus: thanks. timeline wise we're moving fast, we need a vendor decision in 3 weeks.
[00:39] Priya: and i'll be focusing on retention, pii/phi handling, and the exact wording of the no-train clause.
[00:47] Samira: great. high level, redwood provides hosted, dedicated, and private — private being vpc/on-prem. you can pin model versions, and we have a strict policy about data use, we do not train on customer prompt/content by default. we'll go through a written confirmation later in the call.
[01:10] Dr. Elena: can you be specific? what does "not train" mean operationally — like do you retain prompts, are they queued anywhere?
[01:18] Jonas: good question. so by default our hosted api retains logs for X days for debugging and safety at a high level, but for enterprise customers we offer dedicated pools and private control plane options where retention can be set to zero and no training flag is enforced. i know that's a bit jargon-y —
[01:36] Marcus: wait, retention set to zero — does that mean tokens aren't persisted at all? we need to ensure phi doesn't leak or get used elsewhere.
[01:43] Jonas: right — in dedicated + private there are two levers: storage retention and model telemetry. we can disable prompt retention, and we can also turn on a hard no-train policy which prevents ingestion into any training pipelines. logs for billing/alerts can be routed to your SIEM instead of our stores.
[02:05] Priya: is that configurable per-project or per-tenant? we have multiple business units with different regs.
[02:12] Samira: per-tenant. you can scope the policy to the workspace or route.
[02:18] Leo: about encryption — can we use our KMS? we can't have Redwood hold keys.
[02:24] Jonas: yes, customer-managed keys supported for private and dedicated. we do envelope encryption: model secrets and token caches are encrypted with your CMK; we also offer HSM integrations for on-prem/air-gapped. note: some ephemeral caches (kv cache) may be in-memory only and not persisted.
[02:44] Dr. Elena: what's the audit log surface? we require user-level actions, payload hashing, and retention for 7 years for some regs.
[02:52] Jonas: our audit log supports request-level entries, with metadata: user id, workspace, model version, route, timestamp, and action. payload logging is optional and can be hashed or redacted; we can also send logs to your SIEM (syslog, S3, or direct API). retention windows are configurable in private deployments.
[03:12] Marcus: how easy is SCIM provisioning for RBAC? we want role sync from Okta.
[03:18] Samira: we support SSO (SAML/ OIDC) and SCIM for user provisioning. roles map to admin/engineer/viewer etc. we can demo the SCIM sync during the pilot.
[03:28] Priya: can you put the RBAC granularity in writing? we need admin separation and audit trail for admin actions.
[03:34] Jonas: yes — admin actions are logged separately and we keep immutable admin audit events in the private control plane.
[03:41] Dr. Elena: and regarding 'no training' — how do you prove that? is there an attestation?
[03:48] Samira: we will provide a written attestation that we do not use customer prompts to update model weights and will not include customer data in training datasets. for extra assurance we can also provide a runbook of controls and SOC 2 controls mapping.
[04:02] Priya: that attestation needs to be legal text our counsel can sign off on. any prior customers refused? i mean do you have exceptions?
[04:12] Samira: exceptions only with explicit opt-in and contract language for training ingest. default is no.
[04:18] Leo: ok, about network — for private deployment does redwood require open egress to aws? we have strict firewall rules.
[04:25] Jonas: private control plane is customer-managed VPC peering or private link. if on-prem, the inference nodes sit behind your firewall. we can document required egress for remote attestation, if any.
[04:38] Marcus: latency concerns — if we route logs to our SIEM it shouldn't add latency to inference, right?
[04:44] Jonas: logs are asynchronous. no added token latency; telemetry streaming is decoupled.
[04:49] Dr. Elena: can you confirm PHI handling? some prompts may include patient identifiers in testing. we need pseudonymization guidance.
[04:58] Samira: yes, recommended approach is client-side pseudonymization before sending live prompts for the pilot. we can also support a preprocessing layer in your VPC to scrub PII/PHI, or use our built-in redaction rules if you prefer.
[05:15] Priya: what about data residency — we need EU-only for some workloads.
[05:20] Jonas: you can pin region to EU or use private deployment entirely in your EU cloud region. dedicated pools can be provisioned in specific regions and are isolated.
[05:30] Marcus: ok. competitor question: OpenCloud AI told us they do token-level isolation but still use some telemetry for models. how is redwood different?
[05:38] Samira: we focus on clear policy boundaries: no telemetry used for model training unless explicitly contracted. telemetry for reliability may be collected but can be routed out of our stores to yours.
[05:48] Dr. Elena: log format — do you include the actual prompt in logs if we opt-in?
[05:53] Jonas: by default no for enterprise private. for debugging we can include prompt hashes, or full payload if you permit; and again, that can be delivered to your S3 with your KMS key.
[06:05] Leo: KMS rotation — will redwood re-encrypt objects when we rotate keys?
[06:09] Jonas: we support key rotation. for CMK rewraps we can re-encrypt with the new key as part of a maintenance window — details depend on deployment.
[06:18] Priya: can we get a sample contract clause for 'no training' wording?
[06:23] Samira: yes, we'll provide a standard clause and we can adapt based on your legal ask.
[06:28] Marcus: about storage of embeddings — we use embeddings heavily. are they considered persistent and could they be used for training?
[06:36] Jonas: embeddings are treated as customer data; in dedicated/private deployments they are stored per your retention policy and won't be used for training unless you opt-in. we can also not persist embeddings and only keep ephemeral indexes.
[06:49] Dr. Elena: great. let's talk about audit logs detail — we need to see an example row.
[06:55] Jonas: i'll send a sample CSV with fields: timestamp, user_id, workspace_id, request_id, model_version, route, request_hash, response_hash, action, error_code. payload columns are optional.
[07:10] Priya: retention policies — we might need a 7-year store for certain records. can redwood commit to that?
[07:16] Jonas: for private deployments you control retention. for hosted we offer configurable retention tiers but 7 years may require export to your archival store, which we support via S3 export.
[07:29] Marcus: SLAs — what uptime and latency targets do you commit for Dedicated?
[07:34] Samira: Dedicated has an SLA offering; we'll share the SLA doc. typical p99 targets depend on model and pool size — jonas can propose the pool sizing in the pilot.
[07:45] Jonas: yep i'll include recommended GPU pool sizes and the expected p50/p95/p99 numbers for your 512-token average workload.
[07:56] Dr. Elena: about monitoring and alerts — do you integrate with PagerDuty / Opsgenie?
[08:01] Jonas: yes, alert hooks, webhooks, and metrics exports to Prometheus/Grafana stacks; also we can push incidents to PagerDuty.
[08:09] Marcus: any caveats with on-prem? like hardware compatibility?
[08:13] Jonas: on-prem option has a supported list of NVIDIA cards and OS images; we can share the compatibility matrix.
[08:21] Priya: legally we need an attestation and an engineer-signed statement that data is not used for model updates. is that possible?
[08:28] Samira: yes, we provide both an organizational attestation and a technical runbook describing how model update pipelines are walled off.
[08:36] Dr. Elena: ok. for the benchmark pilot — we want to run a 2-hour test with de-identified real prompts against a dedicated pool to validate latency/cost. what do you need from us?
[08:45] Jonas: sample prompt set, target qps, token distribution, network access details, and a contact for the test window. we'll provide benchmark scripts and the pool.
[08:55] Leo: we will need to review firewall rules before the test.
[08:58] Jonas: yes, we'll provide the IP ranges and required endpoints.
[09:03] Dr. Elena: a few clarifying Qs from legal: can you sign a Data Processing Addendum and include the no-training clause?
[09:09] Samira: yes, standard DPA is available and we can add a specific clause for training prohibition.
[09:14] Priya: also, can you provide copies of penetration test reports or third-party attestations?
[09:20] Jonas: we can share redacted pentest summaries and third-party scanner attestations under an NDA; SOC2 and ISO attestation are available for customers.
[09:31] Marcus: are backups encrypted with the same CMK?
[09:35] Jonas: yes, backups follow the same envelope encryption policy and can be encrypted with your CMK.
[09:40] Samira: quick note — sometimes the auto-transcript will say things like "K V cash" for kv cache, so you'll see some weird bits in the transcript we share.
[09:49] Dr. Elena: haha noted.
[09:51] -- discussion continues with case studies and minor clarifications --
[12:30] Jonas: i want to surface a subtle point — model variants. if you need an on-prem/air-gapped model binary, we can provide a vetted model artifact and runtime. that artifact won't phone home unless you enable updates.
[12:44] Priya: great.
[12:47] Marcus: one more question on deletion — if we ask you to delete data, how long until crypto/shred?
[12:53] Jonas: for private infra, deletion is immediate at storage layer and we provide a deletion report. for hosted, deletion requests will purge and we provide audit of purge actions; backups may require additional processes, which we'll document.
[13:06] Dr. Elena: what's included in the deletion report? request id, timestamp, objects removed?
[13:11] Jonas: yes those fields plus operator id and verification signature.
[13:18] Samira: ok, we're approaching time — i'll recap the main asks and next steps.
[13:24] Samira: action items: we'll send SOC2+ISO docs, provide 'no-training' clause, share audit log sample, and jonas will schedule the 2-hour dedicated pilot.
[13:37] Marcus: thanks, expecting the docs by friday.
[13:40] Priya: legal will review the attestation and DPA.
[13:44] Dr. Elena: thanks everyone.
[13:47] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up over e-mail with attachments and calendar invites.
